notes: Not yet reviewed by a person. Generated 2026-10-17 by working/scripts-energy2/build.py from downloads in working/raw/energy2 (Eurostat, Comtrade, FRED, data.gov.sg) and working/raw/energy (CREA).

transit_gas values are FINAL-USE Russian gas, so they should replace (not add to) the CREA pipeline-gas figures of transit countries. Where only CREA destination data exist (2025-2026), the passed_on_shares say how CREA volumes at DEU/SVK/AUT/HUN/TUR/BGR/SRB/BEL map to final users.

Eurostat partner data are by country of origin and exclude pure transit; Austria (all NSP) and Switzerland (not covered) are estimated from consumption x Russian share. Germany and Czechia report Russian origin directly, so the Czech volume is not double counted in Germany.

Countries with no Russian gas in any year: Croatia (by origin; Russian molecules via Slovenia/Hungary appear only in CREA traces), Cyprus, Denmark (by origin; Danish imports from Germany in 2020-21 are in the DEU passed-on shares via CREA), Ireland, Malta.

Prices: realised import unit values (Comtrade, EUR per m3 using 0.73 kg/m3) - Russian pipeline gas in Europe cost EUR 0.20/m3 (2019), 0.13 (2020), 0.32 (2021), 0.97 (2022), 0.50 (2023), 0.37 (2024), 0.38 (2025); 2026 x1.30 (CREA). 1 m3 = 10.55 kWh GCV.

price_index: EUR-based, 2019-2021 average = 1.00, 2026 = Jan-Aug. Divide a nominal EUR flow by the index to get it at pre-war prices. The pipeline-gas index (contract prices) is much flatter than TTF (pipeline_gas_ttf_reference).

fuel_mix_2019_2021: shares of 2019-2021 cumulative imports from Russia (EUR). For pipeline-gas importers whose customs hide Russian gas (DEU, AUT, POL, NLD, FRA, HUN, CHE, FIN, BEL, TUR) the gas value is set to the transit_gas estimate, first from unallocated HS 27 and the rest added to HS 27 and TOTAL. Algeria and Bangladesh use Russia-reported (mirror) exports. Taiwan = Comtrade "Other Asia, nes" (490).

hub_resale: Share of a hub's IMPORTED refined oil products (HS 2710 / Eurostat O4600) that is re-exported to other countries' customs territories. Bunker fuel sold to ships is NOT counted as resale here (it has no destination country in trade data, but the buyers are mostly foreign shipping companies); it is given separately as bunker_share so the model can choose. The proportional method assumes imported and refined barrels are fungible: re-export share = exports / (imports + refinery output); the upper bound is exports / imports (capped at 1), i.e. imported barrels are exported first.
